summary: Generate ONE new D5 mathematical frontier obligation from the current truth-DAG's dependency-ready open edge, as a single independently mergeable increment: one appended X_Frontier task block (formal open statement + permanent code + difficulty/deps/actionable hint) plus exactly one child issue routed to blueprint-then-formalize. This is the flywheel's upstream (decide WHAT to prove next); it is conservative-extension only (append a task, never touch frozen nodes). Fully self-contained; executors need no other file.
applies_when: Conservative router: choose only when the origin issue text unambiguously requests GENERATING/replenishing the next D5 frontier obligation from the current DAG (deciding what to prove next), and exactly one flow matches. POSITIVE FIXTURE: `Generate the next worthy D5 frontier obligation from the current truth-DAG` => choose `frontier-generation`. NEGATIVE FIXTURE (consumption, not generation): `Deliver ONE NEW D5 result: GoldenInt is a UFD` => choose `blueprint-then-formalize`, because a specific result is already named for formalization. OVERLAP FIXTURE: `Generate and immediately formalize the next frontier result` => choose none/plain devloop, because formalization is a second independently mergeable deliverable. AMBIGUOUS FIXTURE: `Improve the theory` => choose none/plain devloop, because it names no generation-of-frontier transaction. Exclude literature intake, paper production, formalization of an already-identified result, and note-only edits.

steps.title: Select one dependency-ready worthy open obligation and post it as a frontier task

content.generator:
Read the origin issue from its source_ref and emit exactly one child issue title and body for this step. The child must deliver ONE atomic, independently mergeable PR that appends ONE new D5 frontier obligation and posts exactly one downstream child issue. Generation and posting are one transaction. All rules are embedded below; do NOT consult any external spec file.

MACHINE OPEN-STATE, NOT RAW SCAN. Do NOT grep for `sorry` or scan files heuristically. The authoritative open/closed/tail state of every node is the DAG-derived state computed by the repository's own machine (`Meta/StrataLint/StrataLint.Engine/Dag/TruthDagConstruction.DeriveState`); use that derived Open set as the candidate universe. A candidate obligation is ELIGIBLE only if the machine marks it Open AND every declaration it depends on is already Closed (dependency-ready); an obligation whose prerequisites are themselves still Open is dependency-blocked and MUST NOT be selected.

WORTH ARGMAX (deterministic). Among eligible candidates, select exactly ONE by machine-computable worth = equally-weighted (novelty x dependency-readiness x structural-payoff x receipt-potential), per the repository worth doctrine (CLAUDE.md 11.20). Novelty: not already attested/derived elsewhere. Structural-payoff: how many downstream open obligations it unblocks (out-degree in the DAG toward Open nodes). Receipt-potential: whether closing it produces a durable truth node. Tie-break deterministically: higher worth, then shallower DAG depth(v) (longest dependency path), then lexicographic GID. State the argmax candidate and the runner-up with their worth vectors so the choice is auditable; never fabricate a numeric score you cannot derive from the DAG.

STABLE DEDUP (must not flood). Before appending or posting, derive the stable identity `frontier-gen:<GID>` of the selected obligation. Scan every `D5/X_Frontier/*.lean` task block and every open issue (via the platform's issue view) for that exact stable key. If the selected GID already owns an open X_Frontier task block OR an open generation issue, produce NO changes and complete as a successful terminal no-op (verified replay), never a duplicate task block, code, or issue. If the eligible set is EMPTY (no dependency-ready worthy obligation), produce NO changes and complete as a deterministic no-op; do NOT fabricate an obligation.

APPEND ONE FRONTIER TASK (conservative extension). In the SAME PR, append exactly one task block to the canonical `D5/X_Frontier/<Name>.lean` target for the selected GID (create the target only if the obligation's stratum has none). The task block carries: the ordinal owner marker `frontier-gen:<GID>;` first; a permanent code allocated as `D5-T0001` when none exist, else one greater than the numerically greatest existing `D5-T####`, zero-padded to four digits (never fill a gap, wrap, or reuse; fail closed at `D5-T9999`); a formal open statement of the obligation (the exact proposition to be proven, as a Lean signature ending in `sorry` or an open-task declaration, matching the F-layer conventions); difficulty estimate; explicit dependency GIDs (all Closed); an actionable hint; and prior-attempt evidence if any. Never modify a frozen node, a Blueprint node, or any other task block; only append.

POST ONE DOWNSTREAM ISSUE. In the SAME PR (or as the PR's declared side-effect), create exactly one child issue whose title/body route deterministically to `blueprint-then-formalize`: title `Deliver ONE NEW D5 result: <human name>`, body stating it asks for ONE NEW D5 result delivered as a SINGLE increment (Lean F-layer + mirroring Blueprint), naming the appended `D5/X_Frontier/<Name>.lean` obligation and its formal statement, and carrying the `frontier-gen:<GID>` provenance marker for dedup. Do NOT also request formalization inline (that is blueprint-then-formalize's job).

EXECUTABLE ACCEPTANCE FIXTURES (TDD: write these RED first, then implement to GREEN). The child issue must require automated fixtures over synthetic DAG states, not a prose checklist:
- GEN-FROM-READY: a synthetic DAG with exactly one dependency-ready worthy Open obligation yields exactly one appended X_Frontier task block (with `frontier-gen:<GID>` + a fresh D5-T code) and exactly one child issue routed to blueprint-then-formalize; no other diff.
- WORTH-ARGMAX: multiple eligible candidates yields selection of the strict worth-argmax; assert the runner-up is NOT selected and the tie-break order (worth, then shallower depth, then lexicographic GID) decides.
- SKIP-BLOCKED: the only candidate is dependency-blocked (a prerequisite still Open) yields zero appended blocks and zero issues (deterministic no-op); it must NOT be selected.
- DEDUP: the argmax GID already owns an open X_Frontier task block or open generation issue yields zero changes, terminal success no-op.
- REPLAY: applying the same trigger against the same DAG twice yields a byte-identical no-op on the second run (no duplicate block, code, or issue).
- EMPTY-FRONTIER: no dependency-ready worthy Open obligation exists yields zero changes, no-op; no fabricated obligation.
Each fixture asserts the exact appended-block count, the exact posted-issue count, the selected GID, the provenance marker, and the absence of every non-selected candidate. TDD/tests live inside the child PR and are written before the implementation.

ATOMICITY & VALIDATION. Exactly one task block and at most one downstream issue may result. Sort any newly added collections with ordinal comparison. Re-running against the same DAG must select the same GID, code, and target and must not append duplicates. Validate: the DAG-derived Open/dependency-ready predicate, the worth argmax determinism, the D5-T code allocation, the GID round-trips and existence checks, and the fixtures. Do not ask the child to duplicate devloop consensus, CI, PR review, or merge gates; devloop provides those. If open-state derivation is unavailable, the eligible set is empty, the selection is non-deterministic, or dedup is unsafe, the child must produce NO changes with a clear WHY; that no-changes is the correct terminal outcome for an empty/ambiguous frontier, not a failure.
